# Independent preliminary review: reflected Brownian affine crossing

Recommendation to root: **zero discovery credit; do not invest in Lean or a manuscript.** The supplied ordinary proof of the scalar equation (6) passes this review. A complete classical-method bridge supports exclusion as a routine adaptation, independently of the unresolved historical-priority question. This is an eligibility recommendation, not an acceptance, ledger change, or claim that the formula has already appeared in a read earlier source.

## Separate gates

| Gate | Finding |
|---|---|
| SOURCE | PASS for equation (6), arXiv:2603.27602v1 p8, with a>=0, b>0, mu>0 and standard variance-t Brownian motion starting at zero, reflected by the Skorokhod map. |
| MATH | PASS as an ordinary mathematical proof, with analytic details reconstructed below. Exact checker diagnostics support only the algebra. |
| SUBSTANTIVE | EXCLUDE as a routine classical characteristic-root/compensation and stopped-martingale adaptation. Full applicable bridge is given below; shortness is not the reason. |
| NOVELTY | HOLD / not cleared. Grandits same-model body remains unread; current registry heads, bodies, capped intervals and historical merge coverage are not cleared. No claim of worldwide priority or already-published exact subsumption. |

Counts are administrative only: 9 additional / 39 total, next 40. Root alone adjudicates, accepts, counts and stages. No credit for any auxiliary identity, endpoint observation, bibliography correction or checker.

## Actual source and literal limits

I read the frozen actual text bodies: Dumaz–Magaldi introduction through p9, especially the Skorokhod definition on pp3–4 and pp7–8; Mayerhofer published Section 2 including Theorem 1 and its proof; Salminen–Yor Section 2 Theorem 3, Corollary 5, and Section 3 Theorem 9 and its bridge proof; and the relevant reflected-diffusion construction of Magaldi's 2024 predecessor pp5–7. Conclusions below depend on these bodies, not catalogue or search snippets. Frozen PDFs and extracted bodies have exact hashes in provenance.json and freeze-before.json.

The target source is https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27602 (fresh 200 at 2026-10-30T04:34:24Z); it still lists only v1, submitted 29 March 2026 09:47:24 UTC. The frozen PDF labels itself v1 and dates the document 31 March 2026. Equation (6) is an infinite series, despite the surrounding prose calling it an integral expression. With alpha=a/b it states

    P(exists t>=0: R^(-a)(t)>=mu+bt)
      = sum_{j>=1} (-1)^(j-1)
        [binom(j+alpha,j)+binom(j+alpha-1,j-1)] exp(-2mu*j*(jb+a)).

The source's immediately preceding Conjecture 1.4 asserts equality of the entire joint laws of two point processes for all a>=0. Its scalar byproduct is weaker. Equality of this one marginal crossing probability does not establish independent exponential gaps, any higher joint marginal, or that conjecture. No such implication is used here. The proof handles arbitrary real a/b>=0, not just integer values. The positive intercept and positive slope are the nondegenerate series domain reviewed; there is no claim for mu=0 or b=0. The source develops other statements for a>-1; those do not enlarge this assigned formula's reviewed drift regime. Absolute value of Brownian motion with nonzero drift is not substituted for Skorokhod reflection.

## Analytic attack and reconstruction

For fixed a>=0,b>0 define

    c_j=(-1)^(j-1) product_{k=1}^{j-1}(1+a/(bk)),
    lambda_j=2j(jb+a), r_j=2(a+jb), s_j=-2jb, v_j=1+a/(bj),
    u(h,x)=sum c_j exp(-lambda_j*h)[exp(r_j*x)+v_j exp(s_j*x)].

1. **Coefficient and derivative convergence.** The logarithm bound log(1+alpha/k)<=alpha/k gives |c_j|<=exp(alpha H_(j-1))<=e^alpha*j^alpha. On h>=mu, 0<=x<=h, the positive exponential is at most exp(-2(j-1)(jb+a)mu). For j>=2 its exponent magnitude is at least b*mu*j^2: the difference is mu*[bj(j-2)+2a(j-1)]>=0. The negative exponential is at most exp(-2j(jb+a)mu). Multipliers v_j are bounded by 1+alpha. A derivative of order p in h and q in x adds at most a constant times j^(2p+q). Thus each fixed derivative order has a summable Gaussian-in-j majorant on this entire unbounded wedge. The j=1 term is a separate bounded smooth term. This proves the stated uniform convergence and bounds; no uniformity over all parameters is needed or claimed.

2. **Regularity at the reflecting and moving boundaries.** A neighborhood of any compact part of the wedge with h>0 retains quadratic decay, even allowing x slightly outside [0,h]. The series therefore defines a smooth local extension there. Restricting to time <=T confines the stopped path to 0<=x<=mu+bT; localization supplies the ordinary smooth Itô hypotheses. No invalid derivative rule based merely on pointwise series convergence is used.

3. **Generator and Neumann boundary.** Both roots satisfy z^2/2-a*z-b*lambda_j=0. Therefore b*u_h+u_xx/2-a*u_x=0. At x=0, r_j+v_j*s_j=0 exactly. This is the correct reflected generator boundary condition, independent of the convention that relates L to semimartingale local time; the support property of dL suffices.

4. **Moving absorbing boundary.** At x=h the two exponents are -2(j-1)(jb+a)h and -2j((j+1)b+a)h. Since c_(j+1)=-v_j*c_j, each negative-root term cancels the next positive-root term. More explicitly, the Nth partial sum equals

       u_N(h,h)=1+c_N*v_N*exp(-2N((N+1)b+a)h).

   The remainder tends uniformly to zero for h>=mu by the same quadratic bound, proving u(h,h)=1. This also verifies no extra alternating sign, boundary constant or terminal term is missing.

5. **Stopped Itô identification.** Let tau be the first equality R_t=mu+bt. Continuous adapted paths and positive initial separation make tau a stopping time and {tau<infinity} precisely the requested crossing event. Applying Itô to u(mu+b(t wedge tau),R_(t wedge tau)) gives no drift or reflection term. The stochastic integrand is bounded on the stopped wedge, so its integral on [0,T] is square integrable with zero mean. Hence

       u(mu,0)=P(tau<=T)+E[1_(tau>T)u(mu+bT,R_T)].

   This needs neither an a priori probability interpretation or positivity of u, nor a uniqueness theorem for an unbounded-domain PDE, nor optional stopping at an unbounded stopping time.

6. **Terminal condition at infinity.** Skorokhod reflection gives exactly R_T=sup_(0<=s<=T)[B_T-B_s-a(T-s)], since the driving path starts at zero. Thus 0<=R_T<=2sup_(s<=T)|B_s| for a>=0. Reflection/Gaussian tails give P(sup_(s<=n)|B_s|>epsilon*n)<=4exp(-epsilon^2*n/2), a summable bound. Borel–Cantelli and ceil(T) comparison imply R_T/T->0 a.s. With h_T=mu+bT, both h_T and h_T-R_T tend to infinity. The positive-root exponent is bounded by -2(a+jb)[(j-1)h_T+(h_T-R_T)], and the negative-root exponent tends to minus infinity as well. On {tau=infinity} every fixed term tends to zero. The wedge majorant permits dominated convergence over j; the uniform bound for u permits dominated convergence in expectation. On {tau<infinity} the indicator eventually vanishes. These observations dispose of the terminal expectation, including the potentially delicate j=1 positive-root mode.

7. **Literal coefficients and a=0.** At x=0 the coefficient is c_j(1+v_j). Write P_j=product_(k=1)^(j-1)(1+alpha/k). Then binom(j+alpha-1,j-1)=P_j and binom(j+alpha,j)=(1+alpha/j)P_j. This yields exactly the source coefficients, including a=0 and j=1. For a=0 the result is 2 sum (-1)^(j-1)exp(-2mu*b*j^2), agreeing with Salminen–Yor Corollary 5. This check alone would not prove a>0.

No substantive gap was found in PROOF.md. In particular its bounded derivative claim, unbounded wedge use, local-time cancellation, telescoping rearrangement and tail argument survive adversarial checks. The independent checker.py proves nine symbolic algebra identities and checks 125 exact rational coefficient/truncated-boundary cases; it performs no simulation and is not a proof of convergence or stochastic identification.

## Complete classical bridge and substantive judgment

Mayerhofer's actual 2019 Section 2 starts with the reflected SDE, the Neumann generator domain, exponential test functions, characteristic roots and stopped Itô martingales for a fixed barrier. It does not state the target affine-barrier formula. Salminen–Yor's actual 2010 arXiv body supplies the driftless affine problem: Theorem 3 is Doob's wedge formula, Corollary 5 gives the exact a=0 crossing series and Theorem 9 computes finite-time distributions via Brownian bridges. It also does not state the a>0 target. Directly changing the drift of the absolute-value representation or citing either theorem as literal subsumption would be wrong.

Here is the complete applicable extension, which is the basis for the routine-adaptation decision. Append the deterministic coordinate h'=b to Mayerhofer's reflected generator; it becomes b*d_h+(1/2)*d_xx-a*d_x. An exponential mode exp(-lambda*h+z*x) requires z^2/2-a*z-b*lambda=0, and the two roots must be paired with coefficients in ratio -r/s to satisfy Neumann reflection. Seed the affine Dirichlet value 1 using a mode constant along x=h. This forces lambda=r and hence r=2(a+b), s=-2b, lambda=2(a+b). Its other root leaves one exponential residual on the absorbing line.

Cancel that residual with a new positive-root mode. If the current positive root is r and negative root is s=2a-r, matching the new boundary exponent requires lambda'-r'=lambda-s. Inserting lambda'=r'(r'-2a)/(2b) and lambda=r(r-2a)/(2b) gives roots r'=r+2b and r'=2a-r; choose the new positive root r+2b. Induction gives r_j=2(a+jb), s_j=-2jb and lambda_j=2j(a+jb). Neumann pairing then forces v_j=1+a/(jb), while absorbing-boundary cancellation forces c_(j+1)=-c_j*v_j. There is no unsolved recurrence or new theorem-strength probabilistic bridge left over. Gaussian series domination and the elementary Brownian sublinearity argument above validate the construction and identify its probability through the same stopped generator method.

Thus the actual additional work is a fully explicit compensation of elementary exponential modes in a classical reflected-diffusion boundary problem, with standard convergence/Itô estimates. No new structural coupling or joint-process mechanism occurs. I independently agree with the worker's **routine classical adaptation** classification under this campaign's explicit exclusion. This is a substantive judgment based on the exhibited bridge, not on the number of proof lines or the fact that the tools are old. A source's explicit open question can have a correct formula proof yet still fail this campaign's novelty/substantiveness threshold. Root may adjudicate that threshold differently; the MATH and SOURCE findings would remain separate.

# Exact target and bounded research

## Primary statement and chronology

Édouard Bonnet, *Answering Related Questions*, arXiv:2501.10633v2,22April2026, Section1.3 p7, Question5 asks whether Sidestep(Triangle Partition,dist_delta,1) is in FP. v1 was submitted18January2025 and retains the same question. Latest arXiv history shows only these two versions. Exact quantifiers: does there exist one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm A such that, for every finite simple labeled G on n=3m vertices, A outputs a graph H on the same vertices and a correct answer for triangle partition in H, with maximum degree of the symmetric-difference graph G△H at most1? A positive answer includes a partition into m vertex-disjoint triangles; a negative answer must be correct. The source's function-problem convention requires a valid solution or nil, not an unverified assertion. Empty order can be handled immediately; it changes no asymptotic question.

Actual v1, latest v2, author-hosted PDF and relevant definitions/Question5 read. Author publications page labels the paper ESA2026. Author PDF has older prose and no authenticated publisher imprint; it cannot certify the ESA version. No publication DOI is invented. The latest accessible version still asks Question5; published-body comparison remains a limit. Receipt URLs, UTC, exact bytes and hashes accompany this packet.

Section4.3 is an existential 'natural problem' request, not selected. Section4.9 all fixed t for K_t minus one edge is not resolved by its small cases. Actual Section5 proofs read: Theorem5.2 decides on bounded tree-independence using the bounded clique size of minimal models, CMSO2 optimization, and then Theorem5.3's structural recognition either finds the forbidden minor or supplies bounded tree-independence; Corollary5.4 combines them. This is reconnaissance/public-resolved small-scope rejection, not a fresh investigation slot or a new discovery. It supplies no all-t theorem here. No unproved extension to t>=6 is asserted.

## Universal exact reformulation

A graph of maximum degree at most1 is a matching plus isolated vertices. Accordingly any permitted edit splits into disjoint added and deleted matching edges. Triangle-partition existence is monotone under edge addition. If H=G-D+A has a triangle factor, then G+A has that factor and obeys the same radius bound. If H has none, G-D has none and obeys that bound. Hence mixed edits are unnecessary, for every order.

Positive neighbors are exactly graphs G admitting a partition into triples each containing at least two G-edges. Necessity: restrict the output triangle factor to each triple; at most one of its three edges can have been added because added edges form a matching. Sufficiency: each such triple is a triangle or contains a spanning3-vertex path; add its unique missing edge when needed. Different triples are disjoint, so these additions form a matching. This is a {P3,K3}-factor, with P3 a subgraph rather than necessarily induced. The reduction does not provide a polynomial-time factor algorithm. No unsupported complexity claim about P3-factor is needed.

Negative neighbors are exactly edge-matchings D in G intersecting the edge set of every triangle factor of G. Indeed a factor survives deletion iff none of its edges lies in D. Thus a blocker must hit every spanning factor, not every triangle. Enumeration has exponentially many choices; a polynomial verifier/constructor for this condition has not been supplied. Reporting nil without proving the blocker property would be circular. These equivalences are uncredited helpers, not a Question5 resolution.

## Sustained attempt and precise method failures

First try: transfer source Theorem6's maximum-matching Hamiltonicity sidestep. Its proof joins matching edges cyclically by at most one added incident edge per vertex. That creates one spanning cycle, not a triangle partition. For the edgeless graph on6 vertices there is no positive radius1 neighbor at all: every radius1 neighbor is a matching and has no triangle. This defeats the all-positive matching construction, while permitting the trivial negative output. The Hamiltonian proof's use of a missing perfect matching as a negative Hamiltonicity certificate also has no direct triangle analogue: disjoint triangles can have no perfect matching. Thus neither branch transfers as stated.

Second try: use source's radius2 triangle construction. Partition vertices into arbitrary triples and add missing triangle edges; each vertex receives at most2 additions, proving radius2 for all graphs. On an edgeless triple every vertex needs2, so this explicit construction cannot establish radius1. The wedge-factor reformulation states precisely the missing spanning-packing step.

Third try: greedily pack wedges and then repair. On the6-vertex path0-1-2-3-4-5, a full wedge factor exists, but choosing wedge1-2-3 first leaves0,4,5 with only edge4-5. Arbitrary greedy choices cannot certify the positive branch; local augmentation would need a new global theorem. This is a method countermodel, not a source refutation.

Fourth try: decide negative-neighbor existence by deleting a matching to leave a vertex in no triangle. This suffices but is not necessary. Let H have edges01,02,12,03,04,34,05,15,35. Its triangles are012,015,034,035: every vertex belongs to a triangle, all triangles use0, so H has no triangle factor. Let G=H+45. Then012 and345 are disjoint triangles covering all vertices. Deleting the single edge45 from G is a permitted negative neighbor, even though every vertex of H remains in a triangle. The local criterion loses genuine blockers.

For any vertex of degree<=3 a local blocker DOES exist: if degree<=2 delete at most one incident edge to leave degree<=1; if degree3, delete one incident edge vu and, if present, the edge between the other two neighbors. These two edges are disjoint and kill all triangles through v. This handles a full easy subfamily only. For degrees>=4 the remaining neighborhood can contain a triangle, which no matching can hit in every edge. No all-graph residual reduction has been proved.

# Independent preliminary review — power-sum domains

Recommendation: **EXCLUDE from this campaign's substantive-discovery credit** as a routine adaptation of the published singular-locus analysis and classical quadric geometry. Root decides. This is not a finding that the endpoint was already printed or that the proof is wrong. SOURCE passes, ordinary MATH passes, SUBSTANTIVE fails in my assessment, NOVELTY remains bounded/HOLD, and formal feasibility is substantial/uninvested. No credit, acceptance, staging or shared changes occur here.

## Scope and source fidelity

For every integer b>2 let p_j=Σ_{i=1}^4 x_i^j and R_b=C[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]/(p_2,p_b). The candidate proves that R_b is a nonnormal domain exactly for b=6k+5 or b=12k+8, k≥1. This is precisely published Remark 3.3(4), not the a=3 question, a rational-coefficient version, or the general regular-sequence conjecture.

I read the full candidate PROOF.md, the actual published Theorem 2.3 and proof, Theorem 3.1 and proof, Lemma 3.2 and proof, and all eight clauses of Remark 3.3 (printed pp52–60), including the computational explanation in (8). The journal PDF retrieved independently at 2026-10-30T04:33:54 UTC is byte-identical to the frozen candidate journal and author copies: SHA256 f1bf659fa79bc7811ee3976f6548c7f232c1f50e0e3df211e481f485daf66045. Exact URL: https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2025/1-2/5.pdf . The DOI is 10.59277/RRMPA.2025.49.71, RRMPA 70 (2025), 49–71. The received date printed in the source is 10 July 2024. The live https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18906 history lists only v1, 27 September 2024 16:45:13 UTC. Crossref lists year 2025 and record creation 12 March 2025; record creation is not an asserted exact publication date. The actual 2025 body retains the conjecture. No arXiv-PDF/journal textual identity is asserted: the matching PDFs are the author-hosted and journal copies.

The closest actual companion body read is Melánová–Sturmfels–Winter, Recovery from Power Sums, arXiv:2106.13981v1: Sections 2–3, including proofs of Proposition 3, Proposition 10, Theorem 13 and Theorem 15, Example 4, Corollary 5 and the discussion of homogeneous systems. The live history gives 26 June 2021 09:31:22 UTC; the cited journal publication is Experimental Mathematics 33 (2024), 225–234, DOI10.1080/10586458.2022.2061650. Proposition 3 is generic radicality/dimension; Corollary 5 is irreducibility of the image, not the zero fiber. Example 4 explicitly has reducible/nonreduced special zero fiber. Theorems 13/15 are finite computations for three-variable systems, not four-variable primality. Thus this body does not already supply the endpoint. Its cached PDF hash is 5e1db1b5795de4f05ec5ef473759f1ad5012fa1171731576ff8818e88d4ac38a. I do not claim to have independently body-read the 2009 CKW paper, Froberg–Shapiro, or every cited predecessor.

## MATH: exhaustive attack and independent reconstruction

The imported radicality has exactly the needed hypotheses: Theorem 2.3(4), n=4,c=2, distinct positive exponents. The proof makes the complete intersection generically regular and then reduced; it is not merely generic-fiber radicality. Theorem 3.1 specializes at a=2 to normal-domain precisely when b≢2 mod4 and b≢2 mod3. For ν3(b)=0, its second alternative succeeds exactly when ν3(b−2)=0; if 3 divides b the first alternative succeeds. These statements exclude all other residues from the requested nonnormal-domain classification, once the exceptional nonprime cases are handled.

Here is the complete applicable classical bridge; the conclusion below does not rest on proof length.

1. Put Q=V(p2)⊂P3. Its quadratic form has rank four, so Q is smooth. Over C choose coordinates giving X0X3−X1X2=0; the Segre map identifies Q with P1×P1. Let A and B be the classes of fibers of its two projections. These generate Pic(Q): a divisor restricts to a principal divisor on A2 because C[u,v] is factorial; subtract that principal divisor and the remaining divisor is supported on the two boundary fibers. Independence follows by degrees on the two fibers. Their intersections are A²=B²=0 and A·B=1 (move fibers, or compute transverse local coordinates). A hyperplane is A+B. Thus C_b=V_Q(pb) has class (b,b). An effective nonzero curve has class (c,d) with c,d≥0, because intersection with general fibers gives nonnegative degrees. Its hyperplane degree is c+d.

2. Use source reducedness. If C_b is reducible, partition ALL of its irreducible components into any two nonempty sets D,E. They share no component, regardless of how many components either contains. Classes are (c,d) and (b−c,b−d), with 0≤c,d≤b, 1≤t=c+d≤2b−1. Intersection is I=b(c+d)−2cd. On a smooth surface, the intersection of two effective divisors without common components is the sum of lengths O_Q,P/(f_D,f_E). This follows by restricting the defining section of E to D and counting its zeros with length; the degree is the class intersection just computed. At a node the completed equation has two distinct smooth tangent branches. If branches are split between D and E, the local ideal is a pair of transverse parameters, length one. If they are in the same part, the other part misses the point. A smooth point cannot lie in both parts. Therefore I≤N for a curve with N ordinary nodes and no other singularities. This deals with arbitrary partitions, not just two irreducible components.

3. Since cd≤t²/4, I≥bt−t²/2. This concave quadratic has minimum b−1/2 on [1,2b−1]; integrality yields I≥b. If there is no line component, D and E each have degree at least two: an effective degree-one divisor is a single ruling line. Now t∈[2,2b−2], giving I≥2b−2. Consequently N<b, or no lines together with N<2b−2, implies irreducibility. Neither hypothesis says simply that a singular curve must be irreducible.

4. Specialize the source's Theorem 3.1 proof, cases (a)–(d), at a=2. Let h=b−2.
